method: Independent direct visual inspection of exactly eight candidate_round2 boards at native, 2x, and 4x scales. No pipeline code, manifests, goal documents, or stored verdict files read. Verdicts concern the requested attachment/object/action categories, not overall sprite art quality.

visible_reasons_by_scale.1x: A small container projects directly from the hip; there is no visible food-to-mouth action.
visible_reasons_by_scale.2x: The tan load stays contiguous with the low arm and has contrasting pale contents.
visible_reasons_by_scale.4x: The shallow basket-like outline and contents read as a low carried food container. The broad flat torso patch is visually crude, but does not suggest eating.

visible_reasons_by_scale.1x: The figure holds a small projecting load low in front; the face is clear of a separate food item.
visible_reasons_by_scale.2x: The container connects at waist/hip height through an orange hand or forearm shape.
visible_reasons_by_scale.4x: A dark-edged shallow container with red and pale contents is attached to the low hand. The torso is conspicuously flat and rectangular, but the gesture now reads as carrying.

visible_reasons_by_scale.1x: The load is clearly at the side, below the face, and the figure no longer reads as eating.
visible_reasons_by_scale.2x: A red-and-tan filled container sits against the right hip with a continuous connection.
visible_reasons_by_scale.4x: The hand/container junction is contiguous and the contents remain inside the dark basket-like outline. The oversized flat orange chest patch is an art-quality weakness outside the four action verdict categories.

visible_reasons_by_scale.1x: Dark blocks flank the hip, but they do not resolve as a recognizable bundle of wood.
visible_reasons_by_scale.2x: The right-hand load looks like a short outlined container with an amber patch, not several bundled lengths of wood.
visible_reasons_by_scale.4x: The black rectangular outline and enclosed brown marks read more like a box or basket than bundled logs. Attachment is substantially clearer, but the carried object identity fails.

visible_reasons_by_scale.1x: The small side container is held low; there is no clear separate food item touching the mouth.
visible_reasons_by_scale.2x: The tan filled container stays joined to the hip-side arm. The red shoulder accent remains, but no longer forms a distinct eating gesture.
visible_reasons_by_scale.4x: The low basket-like load has light contents and a continuous attachment. The large flat orange upper-arm patch is crude, while the hand-to-mouth reading is no longer dominant.

visible_reasons_by_scale.1x: The only obvious carried object is low and ahead of the hip.
visible_reasons_by_scale.2x: The red-and-tan shallow container remains joined to the arm; the face area is separate from it.
visible_reasons_by_scale.4x: The low hand joins the container rim/body without a background gap. The blocky orange torso is visually weak, but the action reads as carrying food rather than eating.

visible_reasons_by_scale.1x: The small side load sits at the hip, with no competing eating gesture.
visible_reasons_by_scale.2x: The filled container touches the low side of the figure in every row.
visible_reasons_by_scale.4x: Red and tan contents are contained in a dark shallow basket-like outline connected at hip level. The broad orange rectangular torso lacks natural arm detail, but the load is not floating or raised toward the mouth.

visible_reasons_by_scale.1x: The first row still has a small load visibly detached on the right; the other rows look more contiguous.
visible_reasons_by_scale.2x: A background gap remains between the right-hand object and the body in row 1, while a hand is raised near the head.
visible_reasons_by_scale.4x: Row 1 shows the right load separated by background from the hip, with no hand touching it; later rows improve attachment. Across the board the short dark outlined objects also remain weak as recognizable bundled wood.
